items.name: Keller relation groupoid and Čech nerve
items.statement: For every complex Keller map f:A^n→A^n, R_f=A^n×_f A^n ⇒ A^n is a thin étale equivalence-relation groupoid and K_r(f) is its Čech nerve.

items.name: Smooth affine parallelizable levels
items.statement: Every K_r(f) and every fiber configuration variety \operatorname{Conf}_k(f) is a smooth affine n-fold with trivial algebraic tangent bundle.

artifact.locator: Proposition 2.2 — Every level is a smooth affine n-fold

items.name: Partition decomposition
items.statement: For every r, K_r(f) is the disjoint union over set partitions π of [r] of C_|π|(f); equivalently K_r≅⊔_k S(r,k) \operatorname{Conf}_k.

items.name: Generic degree bounds configurations
items.statement: If f has generic degree d, no fiber has more than d points and \operatorname{Conf}_k(f)=∅ for k>d.

artifact.locator: Lemma 4.1 — No fiber has more points than the generic degree

items.name: Finite geometric palette
items.statement: Every connected-component isomorphism type occurring anywhere in the Keller nerve occurs among \operatorname{Conf}_1,…,\operatorname{Conf}_d and therefore by finite level d.

items.name: Fiber-cardinality filtration
items.statement: The image of q_k:\operatorname{Conf}_k→A^n is the open locus U_{≥k} of targets with at least k preimages; U_d is the proper locus and its complement is the nonproperness set.

artifact.locator: Proposition 5.2 — Collision images recover the filtration

items.name: Top configuration open immersion
items.statement: The forgetful map \operatorname{Conf}_d→\operatorname{Conf}_{d-1} is an open immersion, and it is an isomorphism iff f has no fiber with exactly d−1 points.

items.name: Monodromy-orbit component theorem
items.statement: If G≤S_d is the monodromy group over the proper locus, connected components of \operatorname{Conf}_k correspond to G-orbits on ordered k-tuples of distinct sheets; \operatorname{Conf}_k is irreducible iff G is k-transitive.
items.reason: the draft records the argument as a reason from standard finite-cover theory

artifact.locator: Theorem 7.1 — Collision components are monodromy orbits

items.name: Top configuration realizes Galois closure
items.statement: Over the proper locus, \operatorname{Conf}_d has d!/|G| connected components, each a Galois cover with group G realizing the Galois closure.

artifact.locator: Corollary 7.2 — The top configuration is the Galois closure

items.name: Stirling additive-invariant calculus
items.statement: For every additive invariant I, I(K_r)=Σ_k S(r,k)I(\operatorname{Conf}_k); Stirling inversion recovers I(\operatorname{Conf}_k), and the sequence I(K_r) satisfies the recurrence with characteristic polynomial ∏_{j=1}^d(T−j).

items.name: Euler factorial-moment identities
items.statement: If U_m is the exact m-point fiber stratum then χ(\operatorname{Conf}_k)=Σ_{m≥k}(m)_k χ(U_m), a triangular system recovering the Euler characteristics of fiber strata.

items.name: Canonical frame and LND criterion
items.statement: Every Keller configuration component has a canonical commuting algebraic frame pulled back from A^n; if all frame derivations are locally nilpotent on a connected component then that component is A^n, and for the source this implies f is an automorphism.

items.name: The diagonal is a connected component
items.statement: For a Keller map f the identity section Δ: A^n → R_f = A^n ×_f A^n is open and closed, so R_f = Δ ⊔ Conf_2(f).

artifact.locator: Proposition 1.3 — The diagonal is a connected component

items.name: Automorphisms are exactly the collision-free case
items.statement: For a complex Keller map f, Conf_2(f) = ∅ iff f is injective iff f ∈ Aut(A^n); the Jacobian conjecture in dimension n says every Keller groupoid on A^n is the unit groupoid.

artifact.locator: Corollary 1.4 — Automorphisms are exactly the collision-free case

items.name: The nerve is 2-coskeletal
items.statement: K_•(f) is the nerve of a groupoid and hence 2-coskeletal: K_1, K_2 and the source/target/composition/unit/inverse maps determine every K_r and every simplicial structure map.

artifact.locator: Proposition 2.4 — The infinite nerve is categorically finite data

items.name: Forgetful configuration fiber count
items.statement: ρ_k: Conf_k(f) → Conf_{k-1}(f) is étale; over a point lying over an m-point fiber its fiber has exactly m−k+1 points, and generically deg ρ_k = d−k+1.

items.name: Normal extensions are forbidden for counterexamples
items.statement: If the function-field extension of f is Galois the monodromy action is regular and |G| = d, and by Campbell's criterion f is then invertible; so a nontrivial Keller groupoid has |G| > d. There is no degree-two complex Keller counterexample, and S_3 in degree three is the first non-Galois possibility.

artifact.locator: Corollary 7.3 — Normal extensions are groupoid-simple and forbidden for counterexamples

items.name: Unordered configuration quotients
items.statement: S_k acts freely on Conf_k(f); B_k(f) = Conf_k(f)/S_k parametrizes unordered k-subsets of fibers, has fiber cardinality C(m,k) over U_m, B_d(f) ≃ U_d is the proper locus, and over the proper locus B_k ≃ B_{d−k}.

items.name: Čech realization recovers the image
items.statement: Since f^an: X^an → U^an is a surjective local homeomorphism, |K_•(f)^an| ≃ U^an, and there is a homological descent spectral sequence E^1_{p,q} = H_q(K_{p+1}(f)^an; Z) ⇒ H_{p+q}(U^an; Z).
items.reason: the draft calls this standard descent machinery rather than a new theorem

artifact.locator: 12. Topological realization of the Keller groupoid

items.name: Vertical homological boundedness
items.statement: Every K_r(f) is a smooth affine n-fold, so by Andreotti–Frankel H_q(K_r; Z) = 0 for q > n; the descent spectral sequence is a strip of n+1 rows.

items.name: Finite homological palette
items.statement: H_q(K_r) ≃ ⊕_{k=1}^d H_q(Conf_k)^{⊕S(r,k)}, so the E^1 page of the descent spectral sequence is built from the homology of Conf_1, …, Conf_d alone.

items.name: Reconstruction from active monodromy data
items.statement: Étale-maximal Keller maps correspond to active monodromy data whose canonical étale filling is affine space; the Jacobian-conjecture counterexample condition is equivalent to existence of a nontrivial active datum whose étale filling contains a dense open A^n.

items.name: Rigidity of extended Rees algebras
items.statement: For a smooth affine complex surface Σ with log Kodaira dimension κ̄(Σ) ≥ 0, every finitely generated extended Rees algebra of a nonzero multiplicative ideal filtration is rigid (equivalently its Makar-Limanov invariant is the whole ring).

items.name: Explicit Keller map is étale and noninjective
items.statement: The displayed polynomial map F : A^3 → A^3 satisfies det JF = -2 and has a fiber containing three explicit distinct points; hence it is étale and noninjective.

semantics.lean_level: internal for determinant and collision; étaleness upgrade is boundary

items.name: Simple-root incidence model
items.statement: The source A^3 is isomorphic to the simple-projective-root locus of the binary cubic Φ_{A,B,C}(S,T)=2AS^3-BS^2T+2ST^2-CT^3; fibers of F correspond to simple projective roots.

semantics.lean_level: set-level equivalence internal; scheme isomorphism assembled via boundary axiom

items.name: Finite incidence normalization
items.statement: The incidence variety is smooth and irreducible; its projection to target A^3 is finite of degree three and its étale locus is exactly the simple-root locus.

semantics.lean_level: boundary/assembled for projective/proper/quasi-finite and irreducibility infrastructure

items.name: Discriminant geometry
items.statement: Δ=B^2-16A-B^3C+18ABC-27A^2C^2 is irreducible; its reduced singular locus Γ≅C* is the triple-root locus; the discriminant hypersurface is smooth off Γ and has transverse cusp singularities along Γ.

semantics.lean_level: mixed: explicit algebra internal; irreducibility and singular-locus criteria at boundary

items.name: Complete fiber census and image
items.statement: Fibers of F have cardinality 3 off Δ=0, cardinality 1 on the smooth discriminant stratum, and cardinality 0 on Γ; therefore F(A^3)=A^3\Γ.

items.name: Nonproperness locus

items.name: One-point stratum isomorphism
items.statement: For T=F^{-1}(V(Δ)), the restriction F|_T : T → V(Δ)\Γ is an isomorphism; in particular T is smooth and irreducible.

items.name: Monodromy is S3
items.statement: The monodromy group of the three-sheeted cover over A^3\V(Δ) is S3.

keller-groupoids-rank-two.title: Keller groupoids and the Jacobian conjecture in rank two

items.name: Fiber deficit decomposes into inertia support plus deletion
items.statement: For a generic point of a nonproperness-curve component C, if sigma_C is generic inertia, m_C is the affine fiber cardinality, and t_C is the number of omitted unramified sheets, then d-m_C = supp(sigma_C)+t_C.

items.name: Deficit-one detects unramified deletion
items.statement: A generic (d−1)-point fiber along a curve component cannot arise from ramification; it forces trivial generic inertia and deletion of exactly one unramified sheet.

artifact.locator: Corollary KG-P2 — deficit one detects non-maximality

items.name: Étale-maximal top configuration stabilization
items.statement: For every étale-maximal degree-d Keller map, there are no (d−1)-point fibers and the forgetful map Conf_d(f)→Conf_{d−1}(f) is an isomorphism.

artifact.locator: Theorem KG-P3 — top stabilization under étale-maximality

items.name: Configuration filtration recovers generic deletion counts
items.statement: The configuration threshold along each nonproperness component recovers its generic affine fiber count m_C; together with inertia this determines the generic unramified deletion count t_C.

artifact.locator: 6. Generic configuration thresholds record inertia support

items.name: Unit-rank lower bound from configuration images
items.statement: If the codimension-one complement of the image of Conf_k has c_k irreducible components, every dominating connected component Z of Conf_k has rank O(Z)^*/C^* at least c_k; in particular top configuration components have unit rank at least the number of irreducible components of S_f.

items.name: Secant projector ideal criterion
items.statement: For a plane Keller map, a polynomial divided-difference determinant yields the diagonal idempotent on K_2; the off-diagonal fiber configuration is cut out by the equal-image equations plus this determinant, and invertibility is equivalent to that ideal being the unit ideal.
items.reason: derived independently in the project, but priority overlaps Collision Ideals and Off-Diagonal Sheets; see notes/roy-van-rijn-provenance.md before this becomes load-bearing

items.name: Boolean equality projectors on the Keller nerve
items.statement: Pairwise diagonal idempotents on K_r form a Boolean equivalence-relation algebra whose primitive idempotents cut out exactly the set-partition configuration components.

artifact.locator: 10. Boolean equality projectors at all levels

items.name: Top configuration failure detects non-maximality
items.statement: If Conf_d→Conf_{d−1} is not surjective, the Keller map is not étale-maximal; its complement consists exactly of ordered (d−1)-tuples over deficit-one fibers.

items.name: Configuration-derived planar exclusion criterion
items.statement: Combine top stabilization, unit-rank/parallelizability, finite-group action, or secant-projector identities with plane-curve boundary data to exclude at least one previously admissible class of hypothetical planar Keller maps.

artifact.locator: 13. Criteria we should now try to turn into exclusions

items.name: Global Euler-deficit identity
items.statement: For a plane Keller map of generic degree d with exact fiber strata U_m, d − 1 = Σ_{m=0}^{d−1} (d − m) χ(U_m); it follows from Euler integration of fiber cardinality on the source and additivity on the target.
items.reason: high-priority human audit

items.name: Purity of the finite-normalization boundary
items.statement: For the finite normalization of a planar Keller map, the complement of the affine-plane source has no isolated points; it is pure divisorial.

items.name: Unramified boundary normalization theorem
items.statement: A boundary divisor generically unramified over the target is étale along its entire curve, is isomorphic to A^1, and maps isomorphically to the normalization of its nonproperness-curve component.

artifact.locator: Theorem EM-2 — generically unramified boundary is everywhere étale

items.name: Multibranch necessity for non-maximality
items.statement: If a planar Keller map is not étale-maximal, some omitted A^1 normalization sheet lies over a singular multibranch component of the nonproperness curve; unibranch singularities cannot support an unramified deleted sheet.

artifact.locator: Theorem EM-4 — unibranch singularities cannot support deletion

items.name: Unibranch criterion for étale-maximality
items.statement: If every irreducible component of the planar nonproperness curve is unibranch at every finite singularity, then the Keller map is étale-maximal.

items.name: Conductor-point fiber bound
items.statement: If an omitted unramified normalization sheet lies over a point where its target curve has r branches, then the affine fiber has at most d−r points; with t such sheets, at most d−tr.

items.name: Connected nonproperness implies étale-maximality
items.statement: If the nonproperness curve S_F of a plane Keller map is connected then F is étale-maximal; equivalently, non-maximality forces S_F to be disconnected. Non-maximality gives a component with normalization A^1 and a multibranch self-identification, so χ(S_F) ≤ 0, against Jelonek's χ(S_F) > 0 for connected S_F.
items.reason: high-priority human audit

artifact.locator: Theorem EM-7 — connected nonproperness implies étale-maximality

items.name: Disconnected components lie in a common rational pencil
items.statement: If S_F is disconnected then every irreducible component is a fiber V(h − a_i) of one polynomial h with a rational one-place pencil, and every connected component of S_F is irreducible.
items.reason: high-priority human audit; re-audited against Assi's actual statements

items.name: Exactly two selected fibers in the noncoordinate case
items.statement: In the situation of KG-EM08 the number q of selected fibers is 2: q ≥ 3 forces h equivalent to a coordinate by Assi's rational-pencil theorem, and a finite union of coordinate fibers misses another coordinate fiber, against the Braun–Dias–Venato-Santos intersection theorem.

items.name: Two-nodal-fiber theorem
items.statement: If a plane Keller map is not étale-maximal then S_F = C_0 ⊔ C_1 with C_i = V(h − a_i) the two exceptional rational members of a noncoordinate one-place pencil; each C_i is rational with one place at infinity, and both have the same positive number of affine singular points, all ordinary transverse nodes. The classification of the two fibers is Assi's; the reduction from Keller non-maximality to it is the project's.
items.reason: highest-priority human audit; never to be described as Assi's theorem

items.name: Eliminate multibranch unramified deletion
items.statement: Exclude omitted unramified A^1 normalization sheets over multibranch singularities of the planar nonproperness curve; this would prove planar étale-maximality.

items.name: Perfect monodromy in the residual non-maximal case
items.statement: Assuming KG-EM10, the sheet-monodromy group of a non-étale-maximal plane Keller map is perfect. The monodromy around a nodal vanishing cycle is σ_+σ_-^{-1} with σ_± conjugate branch-inertia permutations, hence trivial in the abelianization; the load-bearing points are that the vanishing cycles generate H_1 of the generic Assi fiber and that the pulled-back cover's monodromy over that fiber surjects onto the full sheet monodromy.
items.reason: highest-priority human audit

items.name: Forced A_6 node inertia
items.statement: The finite normalization is branched only over C_0; at every node of C_0 the two local branch inertia permutations are disjoint 3-cycles, so the local inertia group is C_3 × C_3.
items.reason: high-priority audit

items.name: No constrained A_6 quotient
items.statement: There is no transitive surjection π_1(A^2 ∖ C_0) → A_6 for an Assi exceptional rational nodal one-place curve C_0 in which geometric meridians map to single 3-cycles and the two branch meridians at every node map to disjoint 3-cycles.
items.reason: the present degree-six model exclusion problem

items.name: Positive-braid conditional exclusion
items.statement: For nodal affine curves the Orevkov invariant is the complement fundamental group (Neumann–Norbury), and it is abelian in the positive-braid-at-infinity case (Orevkov); hence a positive-braid Assi fiber admits no A_6 quotient of the required kind.
items.reason: conditional: whether Assi's exceptional geometry forces positivity is open

items.name: Ramanujam–Morrow boundary recognition
items.statement: For a smooth projective SNC completion U=Y\D, U≅A^2 iff (Y,D) is boundary-birational to (P^2,L∞) by blowups/blowdowns supported on the boundary.
items.reason: llm proved modulo the published Ramanujam–Morrow recognition

artifact.locator: Theorem BG-1 — Boundary-birational recognition of A^2

items.name: Weighted-graph certificate criterion
items.statement: If Y is a smooth projective rational surface, D an SNC divisor of smooth rational curves with connected dual graph, the number of boundary components equals ρ(Y), and a finite legal sequence of weighted boundary blowup/blowdown moves carries Γ(D) to the one-vertex graph [+1], then Y ∖ D ≅ A^2; conversely every SNC completion of A^2 admits such a certificate.

items.name: Affine-plane boundary numerical obstruction package
items.statement: Any SNC completion of A^2 has rational-tree boundary E with r=rho(Y), intersection form of signature (1,r−1) and determinant (−1)^(r−1), K_Y^2=10−r, Euler complement 1, and S^3 plumbing at infinity.

items.name: Topological recognition of A^2
items.statement: A smooth complex affine surface is isomorphic to A^2 if it is contractible and simply connected at infinity, and conversely; for a candidate Keller source a rational-tree boundary generating H_2(Y) gives acyclicity, π_1 = 1 then gives contractibility, and simple connectivity at infinity is the remaining test.
items.reason: llm proved modulo the published Ramanujam characterization

items.name: Inertia-decorated SNC cover reconstruction
items.statement: After resolving the plane branch divisor to SNC, meridian inertia labels commute at nodes; in characteristic zero the normalized finite cover is locally tame/Kummer-toroidal and its resolved boundary graph is algorithmically computable from the resolved graph and finite inertia data.

items.name: Decorated-curve-to-A2 decision with specified deletion data
items.statement: Given a decorated plane curve datum and explicit deletion data specifying the Keller source inside the finite normalization, normalization/resolution followed by the Ramanujam–Morrow boundary test gives an exact decision whether the resulting open surface is A^2.

artifact.locator: KG-P10 — Exact decision with deletion data

items.name: One-place irreducible nonproperness components
items.statement: Each irreducible component of a planar Keller nonproperness curve has normalization A^1 and hence exactly one place at infinity; all such places map to the single projective point at infinity of the whole curve.

artifact.locator: Derived consequence L2a — one place per irreducible component

items.name: Delta-sequence compression of infinity data
items.statement: For each irreducible nonproperness component, its one-place infinity resolution data can be encoded by a finite Suzuki/Abhyankar-Moh delta-sequence; the weighted minimal resolution graph at infinity is determined by this sequence.

artifact.locator: 4. Replace the branch at infinity by a delta-sequence

items.name: Derived affine singularity budget
items.statement: For each rational one-place component of degree m, the total affine delta-invariant is ((m−1)(m−2))/2 minus the delta contribution at infinity, so total affine singularity complexity is derived from the infinity data and degree.

artifact.locator: 6. Affine singularity budget is not free
